Vijay Kumar Gautam vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
Lko on 10 July, 2024

Author: Pankaj Bhatia
Bench: Pankaj Bhatia
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 7450 of 2024
Applicant :- Vijay Kumar Gautam

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
Counsel for Applicant :- Atul Verma,Akhilendra Pratap Singh,Vinod Kumar Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.128 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 302 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Husainganj, District Lucknow.
3. In terms of the FIR it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was married to the applicant in the year 2014 and subsequently, the entire matrimonial family used to harass her.
It was also alleged that on 21.06.2021, the daughter of the informant was beaten and was sent outside the matrimonial home, for which, an information was also given, however, no FIR was lodged.
Subsequently, on account of a settlement, the victim went along with the applicant and thereafter on 16.07.2022, the daughter of the informant was killed.

sentences.text: In the light of the said allegations, it is argued by the Counsel for the applicant that as per the postmortem report, the cause of death is ante mortem head injury allegedly inflicted by the applicant by the use of lathi-danda after taking intoxication.

He further argues that the statement of the informant has already been recorded, wherein, she had specifically stated in the cross-examination that there was no demand of dowry and no allegations were levelled by the informant on that count.
It was also admitted that the applicant had taken the victim to the hospital along with his family members.

It is argued that the entire case is premised on husband attacking the wife after taking intoxication and the applicant has suffered pretrial detention since 23.07.2022 and out of the 18 witnesses, only two have been examined, who are the main witnesses for prosecution to establish the offence.

He further argues that for the sake of argument even if the allegations are treated to be correct, the same would not be an offence under Section 302 of IPC and in fact would fall under Section 304 of IPC.
He also argues that the applicant would also entitled to the benefit of general exceptions contained in Section 85 of the IPC.

He lastly argues that the applicant has suffered sufficient pretrial detention and there is no likelihood of the trial being concluded in near future, as such, the application may be enlarged on bail.

5. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer by arguing that the applicant had committed the murder of his own wife and from the applicant, the Danda allegedly used for causing injury, was recovered, even in the statement of the two witnesses, they have supported the prosecution story, as such, the bail application deserves to be rejected.

6. Considering the submissions made at the bar, prima facie, the marriage was solemnized in the year 2014; the allegation of the applicant being a drunkard are there in the FIR and even in the statement recorded during trial, there are no allegation of demand of dowry as admitted by the PW-1 in the cross-examination.
The issue whether the offence under Section 302 or 304 of IPC is to be decided at the time of trial.
Similarly the benefits of Section 85 of the IPC has also to be considered at the time of trial.

Considering the fact that two main witnesses, who are the fact witnesses, have already been examined and the applicant has no criminal history and thus, there is no martial to suggest that the applicant if enlarged on bail can be any adverse effect of trial, as such,
I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
